findings.highlight: When I came to, I was lying in a burning field.
findings.evidenceJa: —気が付けば、焼け野原にいた。
findings.governingReading: When awareness returns, Shirou finds himself in a burnt-out expanse.
findings.explanation: A burnt-out field becomes a burning field in which Shirou is lying.

findings.highlight: I was the only one left alive.
findings.evidenceJa: この周辺で、生きているのは自分だけ。
findings.governingReading: Within this surrounding area, Shirou perceives himself as the only person alive.
findings.explanation: The only living person in the immediate area becomes simply the only one left alive.

findings.highlight: It wasn't a feeling of disgust...
findings.evidenceJa: ……きっと、ああはなりたくない、という気持ちより。
findings.governingReading: His movement was not simply driven by the feeling that he did not want to end up like the charred people around him.
findings.explanation: Not wanting to become like the burned bodies becomes lack of disgust.

findings.highlight: I took one final deep breath and looked up at the rain clouds.
findings.evidenceJa: 最後に、深く息をはいて、雨雲を見上げた。
findings.governingReading: Unable to breathe properly, Shirou lets out one final deep breath and looks at the rain clouds.
findings.explanation: A final deep exhalation becomes taking a deep breath.

findings.highlight: Light stabbed at my eyes when I woke.
findings.evidenceJa: 目を覚まして光が目に入ってきただけだったが、そんな状況に慣れていなかった。
findings.governingReading: He merely wakes to light entering his eyes but is unaccustomed to such a situation.
findings.explanation: Ordinary waking light and unfamiliarity become light stabbing Shirou's eyes.

findings.highlight: As my eyes adjusted, I woke, alarmed.
findings.evidenceJa: 目が慣れてびっくりした。
findings.governingReading: Once his eyes adjust, Shirou is startled by the unfamiliar hospital room.
findings.explanation: Eyes adjusting and surprise become a second awakening.

findings.highlight: His hair was disheveled, his suit tattered.
findings.evidenceJa: しわくちゃの背広にボサボサの頭。
findings.governingReading: The visiting man has a rumpled suit and disheveled hair.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu's wrinkled suit becomes a tattered one.

findings.highlight: I just accepted his words as fact...I took it neither as a joke or genuine statement.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺はその、冗談とも本気ともとれない言葉を当たり前のように信じて、
findings.governingReading: Young Shirou naturally believes words that could be taken either as a joke or as serious truth.
findings.explanation: Believing an ambiguous claim becomes a contradictory fact statement.

findings.highlight: I guess I said something like that, eyes wide in astonishment.
findings.evidenceJa: 目を輝かせて、そんな言葉を返したらしい。
findings.governingReading: Shirou apparently replies with his eyes sparkling at Kiritsugu's claim.
findings.explanation: Eyes shining with delight become eyes wide in astonishment.

findings.highlight: You can say that...
findings.governingReading: The narrator uses a short 'and, well' transition before judging both Kiritsugu and himself.
findings.explanation: A discourse pivot becomes an incomplete English clause.

findings.highlight: But I was no better, the way I so eagerly bought into it.
findings.evidenceJa: それが羨ましくって目を輝かせた俺も俺だと思う。
findings.governingReading: Shirou judges himself equally absurd because the magic claim made him envious and lit up his eyes.
findings.explanation: Shirou's envious admiration becomes gullibly buying into Kiritsugu's claim.

findings.highlight: I may have been alone in the mansion, but Kiritsugu's stories always helped lessen that.
findings.evidenceJa: いつも屋敷で一人きりだったが、そんな寂しさは切嗣の土産話で帳消しだった。
findings.governingReading: Although Shirou was always alone in the mansion, Kiritsugu's stories canceled out that loneliness.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu's travel stories canceling loneliness becomes merely lessening it.

findings.highlight: Then again, Fuji-nee is brutal when she's the one waking me up, so I prefer you do it. ...Yep, I've learned my lesson. I'll try not to sleep in here next time."
findings.evidenceJa: けど藤ねえにはたたき起こされるから、桜の方が助かる。……うん、これに懲りずに次は頑張る」
findings.governingReading: Shirou sleepily says he will try harder next time without being discouraged by this, leaving the effort unspecified.
findings.explanation: The English supplies a specific promise about where Shirou sleeps and changes his muddled resolve into having learned a lesson. Sakura's enjoyment of waking him is still present.

findings.highlight: Sakura is practically bouncing with excitement.
findings.evidenceJa: 弾むような声で桜は言う。
findings.governingReading: Sakura speaks in a voice that seems to bounce with liveliness.
findings.explanation: Sakura's buoyant voice becomes her body bouncing.

findings.highlight: ...That's odd. Sakura is weirdly energetic this morning.
findings.evidenceJa: ……珍しい。本当に、今朝の桜は元気があって嬉しそうだ。
findings.governingReading: Shirou finds it genuinely unusual that Sakura is so energetic and looks happy this morning.
findings.explanation: Sakura being energetic and happy becomes merely weirdly energetic.

findings.highlight: "No, no. I'm getting up, honest, so let's head to the kitchen together."
findings.evidenceJa: 「ばか、そういう訳にいくか。今起きるから、一緒にキッチンに行こう」
findings.governingReading: Shirou lightly calls Sakura an idiot for offering to do everything, refuses, and asks her to go to the kitchen together.
findings.explanation: Shirou's affectionate 'idiot' disappears.

findings.highlight: The coveralls I wear while I'm working are usually dirty. Who knows what Fuji-nee would say or do if I went into the house as-is.
findings.evidenceJa: 作業着であるツナギは所々汚れている。こんな格好のまま家に入ったら、それこそ藤ねえになんて言われるか。
findings.governingReading: The coveralls are stained here and there from last night's work, making entering the house in them invite Taiga's reaction.
findings.explanation: Currently stained coveralls become work clothes that are usually dirty.

findings.highlight: My old man wasn't from a notable family, yet for some reason he owned this giant house.
findings.evidenceJa: 切嗣は町の名士だった訳でもないのに、こんな広い家を持っていやがった。
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu was not a person of standing or a local notable, making ownership of the large estate puzzling.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu not being a local notable becomes not coming from a notable family.

findings.highlight: So things like inheritance, property taxes, and any other complicated things are all handled by Old Man Fujimura.
findings.evidenceJa: 相続税とか資産税だとか、そういった難しい話は全て藤村の爺さんが受け持ってくれている。
findings.governingReading: Old Man Fujimura handles difficult practical matters such as inheritance tax and property tax.
findings.explanation: Inheritance tax becomes inheritance in general.

findings.highlight: Old Man Fujimura is a major businessman who lives nearby.
findings.evidenceJa: 藤村の爺さんは近所に住んでいる大地主だ。
findings.governingReading: Shirou identifies Old Man Fujimura as a major local landowner after explaining his help with property administration.
findings.explanation: 'Major businessman' replaces the specific fact that Fujimura is a major landowner. This belongs in a dossier on local background or property, rather than Taiga's characterization.
